design: SCRR — Shock-Cohort Residual Reversal: event-gated (|z_e|>=2.5 AND (RZ>=2 OR VZ>=2), cascade flag DZ>=1.5 & >=8 triggers), hold-to-horizon (h=3 primary) long-the-losers cohort on the PIT 273-asset true-daily OHLCV panel, beta-hedged with a BTC spot-margin short (Arm A) or long-loser/short-winner within cohort (Arm B); learned object = hierarchical partial-pooled slope kappa_h(RZ,VZ,DZ,sign) on event rows (secondary monotone depth-3 GBM); analytic DRO gate m_i − sqrt(delta)·se − c_i > 0; one-shot Markowitz size; scored by "unmodified trader.backtest.cell_metrics at H=1" at 21/30 bp plus a declared short-carry term; two-stage kill (Stage 0 kappa table on 2018-10→2023-12, Stage 1 book with one touch of 2024-01→2026-06 and a full-span 2019-2026 CI).
lens: REPO-RECORD CONFLICT — refute from the repository (LEDGER 813/816/819/887/892/897/898, the three consultation entries, TASK_915, trader/config.py, trader/strategy.py, trader/backtest.py, trader/data.py, docs/pathway.md:9-21). Default refuted=true if uncertain.
strongest_objection: The instrument the design inherits is biased in FAVOUR of exactly this signal, and the design's Stage-0 pass threshold sits inside the bias. `trader/data.py:168-187` builds the daily close as the CLOSE OF THE LAST TRADED 1-MINUTE BAR of the UTC day (1-min rows exist only for traded minutes — `trader/backtest.py:76-82` ffill convention), and the scorer enters AT that close: `regime_series` takes fwd = logc[t+H] − logc[t] on the same row that defines the event (`trader/backtest.py:219-224`; `runs/819_single_asset/POWERED_RESULT.md:82` flags "signal at close(t) executes AT close(t)… optimistic only if signals flip intrabar" — harmless for 30-day trend, maximal-harm for a shock-reversal entry). A −12.5% shock day on an illiquid alt closes on a single print that is disproportionately at the bid; the next-day "reversal" therefore contains +half-spread mechanically. With alt spreads of 100–400 bp on cascade days (unmeasured anywhere in the record — 907 captured BTC/USD only; grep finds no alt spread number), the pure-bounce kappa is 0.04–0.16 — the design's S0 PASS bar (kappa_3 >= 0.08) is inside that range, on precisely the "smaller, less liquid pairs" where Bianchi et al. say the premium lives. This is not a speculative worry: Cox & Peterson (1994, JF 49(1), abstract fetched from IDEAS/RePEc): "the bid-ask bounce and the degree of market liquidity explain short-term price reversals… we do not find evidence consistent with the overreaction hypothesis… securities with large one-day price declines perform poorly over an extended time horizon" — i.e. the equity version of THIS effect (the design's Bremer–Sweeney anchor, whose own abstract says the reversals are "potentially lacking profit-making potential") dissolved into the artifact the repo scorer bakes in. Second half of the objection: the design's per-event economics omit the hedge's taker fee (the scorer charges |Δpos| on every column including BTC, `backtest.py:224`), so the corrected round trip per unit hedged long is ≈111 bp, not 42; the statement-of-need's "kappa 0.10 on ~90 cohorts/yr" branch is dead by arithmetic and the mechanism needs kappa_3 ≈ 0.18–0.20 — exactly the magnitude Cox–Peterson attribute to bounce + liquidity. Stage 0 as written would return an uninterpretable PASS; Stage 1 as written would then burn 2–3 implementer-days on it.
arithmetic_check: Identities that hold: SR_yr = SR_e·sqrt(K) for a book flat outside K independent cohorts (mean Kμ/365, var ≈K(σ²+μ²)/365, sqrt(365) cancels) — correct to first order; SD(annual SR) ≈ 1/sqrt(T): 0.63 (2.5 yr) → CI half-width 1.24, 0.37 (7.5 yr) → 0.72 — correct; BBLZ E[max SR_N|H0] with N=36: Φ⁻¹(0.9722)=1.915, Φ⁻¹(0.9898)=2.319, weighted 2.148 → SR0(36)=1.35 / 0.79 — correct; cohort factor sqrt(12/(1+11·0.25))=1.79 — correct; slope power t≈1.8 (150 dates) to ≈8 (3000 independent events) — correct; fee drag 16 units×21 bp=3.4%/yr ≈0.27 Sharpe on a 12.5%-vol book — correct IF the 0.2 cohort gross includes the hedge, which then makes the long legs 0.1 and contradicts the per-position table's base. ERRORS: (1) Hedge fee omitted. Design's own rule ("any SHORT leg: 2×21 bp + h·borrow") is not applied to the BTC hedge, which is charged only 18–36 bp borrow; the scorer charges it 21 bp/side (`backtest.py:224`). Corrected cost per unit hedged long (β shrunk to ~1): 42 + 42β + 27β ≈ 111 bp. Break-even kappa on a 12.5% shock = 1.11/12.5 = 0.089 (zero Sharpe). SR_pos = (kappa·12.5% − 1.11%)/10%: kappa 0.10 → 0.014 (design 0.083); kappa 0.20 → 0.139 (design 0.21). SR_e (×1.79): 0.025 / 0.25. K for +0.97: (0.97/0.025)² ≈ 1500 cohorts/yr (impossible: 60–120 event dates/yr) vs 15 at kappa 0.20; K for +0.56: ≈500 vs 5. Every "kappa 0.10" clause in the statement of need is false; only the kappa ≥0.18–0.20 branch survives, and it needs ≥15 cascade cohorts/yr in 2024–26, where the design itself says cascade days were fewer. (2) Delisting tail understated under the proposed scorer: gross = Σ pos·(log c_{t+H} − log c_t) (`backtest.py:219-223`, tactics-panel correction 2). At w=2.5%, a −95% day costs 0.025×3.0 = 7.5% of book and a −99% day 11.5%, not the "2.4%" quoted (that is the simple-return/hold-shares bound). A 2022-type cluster of 5–10 such names is −40..−100% in the scorer's log units, not −10..−20%. (3) Full-span power overstated: event supply 2018-10→2020 is ≈0 — POWERED coverage shows 12.8 (BEAR18) / 25.2 (REC1920) mean live assets (`POWERED_RESULT.md:28-38`), so the ≥8-trigger cascade flag essentially cannot fire before 2021; informative span ≈2021→2026-06 = 5.5 yr → SD 0.43, half-width 0.84, SR0(36) ≈ 0.92 (and `cell_metrics`' FULL CI is 2021-01→2025-09 = 4.67 yr → half-width 0.91). (4) Event-rate 1–1.5% is plausible (Gaussian P(|z|≥2.5)=1.24%, fat tails higher; RZ≥2 is near-automatic on a 12.5% day) — fine, but asset-events cluster onto ~60–120 dates so "thousands of informative rows" is ~100–150 independent draws/yr, which the design's own date-clustered t already concedes. (5) Borrow arithmetic (0.02%/4h = 12 bp/day) and 3-day sd (6%·√3 ≈ 10%) check out.
profit_source_check: Stated source: FORECAST of the conditional first moment of the h-day market-residual return after a same-day liquidity shock (Nagel-style liquidity-provision premium), with second moments only as conditioners. Framing is internally honest (not a rebalancing premium — no rebalancing; not a market premium — hedged), but three components hide inside the measured number: (a) a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, not a forecast — the bid-ask bounce in the shock-day last-print close (see strongest objection), which is uncapturable because the live entry pays the ask; under the proposed instrument it is indistinguishable from kappa; (b) a MARKET-TIMING component through the hedge — a BTC short held 3 days after cascade days with a beta estimated on 90 calm days; in 2022 (LUNA/3AC/FTX) BTC continued down after cascade days, so hedged-book PnL carries BTC's post-cascade drift whenever β is mis-sized, which the design concedes is "worst exactly on cascade days"; the paired hedged/unhedged report is a diagnostic, not an attribution; (c) the "cost avoidance" claim is real but the design under-counts the cost it avoids by ~2.6× (hedge fee). Is it a forecast in disguise of something already measured dead? Partly: the minute-scale reversal is measured real-but-cost-bound (806 persistence IC −0.052/−0.083/−0.073 at 1/5/20 min, `runs/806_predictability_probe/result.md:31,61,91`; 897 0/864; Kitron 2026) and the design correctly separates itself from it; the unconditional daily residual reversal is in TASK_915's F1 grid and unmeasured; BUT the daily-scale post-vol-shock DIRECTION has a weak mirror reading in the record the design says does not exist (813 B3/B1 continuation cells, see record_conflicts) — negative for reversal at 1 d, weakly positive at 4 d, 33–88 bp/fire, an order of magnitude below the kappa 0.18–0.20 scenario the corrected arithmetic requires.

surviving_mechanism: Only a Stage-0 MEASUREMENT survives, and only in an amended form; no book. Measure, on the PIT daily OHLCV panel 2021-01→2026-06 (2018-20 has no event supply), the date-clustered residual-reversal slope kappa_h (h∈{1,3,5}) after |z_e|≥2.5 ∧ (RZ≥2 ∨ VZ≥2) shock days, with the forward return started from the FIRST TRADED PRINT of day t+1 (from the minute table) — and separately from close_t — so the close_t→first-print gap on event assets is reported as the explicit bid-ask-bounce estimate; event-vs-non-event contrast; loser-only vs winner-only; rank-residual event definition as the primary (removes cascade-day beta error); circular-shift null; the event indicators handed to TASK_915 as F3 features regardless of outcome. It is a 915 appendix (2 CPU-hours inside 915's data build), not a row. A trading mechanism is licensed only if the bounce-robust kappa_3 ≥ ~0.18–0.20 on ≥15 distinct cascade dates/yr in 2021–2023 AND the 2024-26 slope holds sign at ≥50% magnitude — with the hedge charged 21 bp/side and the scorer's log-space tail reported. The 'kappa ≈0.10 on many cohorts' branch is dead by arithmetic under the repo scorer.
kill_experiment_critique: (1) Instrument mis-stated: cell_metrics cannot score 2019-20, 2026H1 or per-year windows and CIs only FULL 2021-01→2025-09 (`config.py:72-79`, `backtest.py:264-275`); window_metrics builds its own positions (`:339`). Use `experiments/898_trend_decay/decay_harness.py:score_window` (pos-matrix, proven byte-identical to window_metrics primitives) and say so; hold-shares needs a NEW PnL path (budget it or drop the claim). (2) Stage 0 is not bounce-controlled: the S0 statistic (kappa on close_t→close_{t+h}) inherits the last-print same-close entry (`data.py:183`, `backtest.py:219-224`); pre-register the forward return from the first traded 1-min print of day t+1 (or a 30–60 min VWAP) as PRIMARY and close_t as the bounce-inclusive diagnostic; report the gap per liquidity decile. Without this, S0 PASS is uninterpretable and the design's own 'S0 PASS → build' rule wastes the implementer days. (3) Replace 'kappa_3 ≥ 0.08' by a cost-anchored bar: kappa_3·mean|e| − (42 + 42β + h·borrow·β) bp > 0 with date-clustered t≥3 on bounce-robust entry; restate the statement of need at kappa ≈0.18–0.20. (4) Charge the hedge in the per-event table (the scorer already does); make the cohort gross base consistent between the economics and the turnover paragraphs. (5) Report the delisting tail in the scorer's log units (7.5–11.5% of book per capped name at −95/−99%), or cap in log space. (6) Redo power for the informative span (2021→2026H1, ~5.5 yr: half-width 0.84, SR0(36)≈0.92) and drop 'full span 2019'. (7) Pre-declare that under `docs/pathway.md:9-21` the row can at best return MARGINAL (unseen-window CI lo>0 needs SR>1.24) and ask the planner to rule whether a default-flat book satisfies 'holds positions' BEFORE the SPEC is hashed. (8) Cite 813's B3/B1 continuation cells as the prior for the horizon choice (h=1 reversal negative gross; h=4 weakly positive, 33–88 bp/fire) instead of 'unmeasured'. (9) Pin the agg1m→kraken_rest source seam (2026-03-31) for range/volume, not a missing 899 backfill. (10) Route O/H/L/V through present_mask BEFORE computing trailing medians (893 prefix hazard, `data.py:113-120`). (11) Rank-residual events as primary, OLS-β events as sensitivity (the design has this inverted). (12) Fold S0 into TASK_915's data build as an appendix — on FAIL its only output is F3 features for 915, on PASS it still needs 915's IC/N_eff frame to be convertible to a Sharpe bound.
odds_after_refutation: P(goalposts: +0.97 net@21 on unseen years with CI lo>0, BEAR-positive, holds positions) ≈ 2–4% (design said ~7%); the unseen-window CI clause alone is unattainable for any SR<1.24 on 2.5 yr, so the honest ceiling of this row is a MARGINAL/paper-candidate verdict. P(amended Stage 0 passes honestly — bounce-robust kappa_3 ≥ 0.08 with date-clustered t≥3, clearly above non-event days, 2021–2023) ≈ 20–30% (design 40–50%: the bounce-robust estimate is smaller, 813's mirror cells are weak/mixed, Cox–Peterson's longer-horizon underperformance of decliners cuts against loser-longs). P(kappa_3 ≥ 0.18–0.20 on ≥15 cascade dates/yr, the only branch that clears cost with the hedge charged) ≈ 8–12%. P(hold-out 2024-01→2026-06 Arm A book ≥ +0.56 net@21 with hedge fee and shock-day slippage) ≈ 5–8%. Value of running the amended Stage 0 inside TASK_915: high relative to cost (2 CPU-hours, zero GPU); value of building the book on the design's current S0 criterion: negative.
